title: The mustard seed and the yeast (Matthew 13:31–33)
hookLine: the smallest seed becomes a bush for birds; a pinch of yeast lifts a mountain of dough

lines: A LUMP OF YEAST. A HEAP OF FLOUR.
cards: A man plants a mustard seed, a speck you could lose under a fingernail. It grows until it's bigger than everything else in the garden, like a small tree, and birds settle in its branches.

A woman making bread works a little lump of yeast into a huge heap of flour, covers it, and leaves it. Slowly, while nobody's watching, the whole heap rises. Two stories, each about as long as a breath.
And Jesus says: this is what the kingdom of heaven is like.

teach.b: Leaven is the old word for yeast, or for a lump of sour dough kept back from yesterday's batch to start today's.
The King James: "The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened." Three things hide in that sentence. First, hid.

teach.h: HID: YOU CAN'T SEE IT WORK.
teach.b: You can't see leaven work; for hours nothing seems to happen. Second, three measures. In Genesis, that's what Abraham asks Sarah to bake when three strangers turn up at his tent: bread for honored guests.
A feast, from one small lump. Third, a surprise. At Passover, Jewish families clear leaven out of the house, remembering bread baked in haste on the way out of Egypt.
And elsewhere Jesus uses leaven as a warning, something spreading where you don't want it. Here he turns it around: the quiet thing that spreads through everything is the kingdom.
The mustard seed does the same trick in the open. The text calls it "the least of all seeds," and says it becomes a tree where "the birds of the air come and lodge."
Gardeners know smaller seeds; the story talks the way a farmer does, about the speck in his palm. So the point comes twice: in a field and in a kitchen, by a man and by a woman.

teach.h: SMALL ENOUGH TO MISS. BIG ENOUGH TO SHELTER.
teach.b: What God is doing, Christians say, starts small enough to miss, grows quietly, and ends up big enough to shelter others.

how: Christians hear these two short parables read together in church, and many see in them a picture of how faith and the church grow: quietly, from small beginnings. Some keep a mustard seed as a reminder.

games.q: you've worked a little lump of leaven into three measures of flour. you cover it and walk away. what happens?
games.why: "till the whole was leavened." a small, hidden thing lifts the whole batch.

practice: Close your eyes and think of one small good thing that could be done quietly, with no one knowing it was you: a counter wiped, a kind note left to be found, the next coffee paid for. Hold it hidden, like leaven in flour.
Then let the picture go, breathe, and let it rise on its own.

wordCard.voice: Leaven. A little lump of yeast, hidden in the dough, that lifts the whole batch.
